content: Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of timolol by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but it is considered minor. Ciprofloxacin may also rarely decrease beta-blocker levels. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of triazolam by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of vitamin K1 (phytomenadione) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is considered minor with unknown clinical significance. Ciprofloxacin enhances the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of acebutolol by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Ciprofloxacin may also rarely decrease beta-blocker levels. Ciprofloxacin and albuterol both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and alfuzosin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Alosetron is associated with serious, potentially life-threatening gastrointestinal adverse effects, and concomitant use with CYP1A2 inhibitors should generally be avoided. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of alprazolam by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of amifampridine through an undefined mechanism. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and coadministration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and aminolevulinic acid (oral) increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period. Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (topical) through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of photosensitizing drugs may enhance the phototoxic reaction to photodynamic therapy with aminolevulinic acid. Ciprofloxacin and amiodarone both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. Ciprofloxacin and amisulpride both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if coadministered. Ciprofloxacin and anagrelide both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ciprofloxacin and arformoterol both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and aripiprazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and arsenic trioxide both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. Ciprofloxacin and artemether both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. Ciprofloxacin and artemether/lumefantrine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of asenapine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and asenapine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Buffered aspirin may decrease the absorption of ciprofloxacin. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after buffered aspirin. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and atomoxetine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is considered minor with unknown clinical significance. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotics may diminish the therapeutic effects of BCG. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. Ciprofloxacin and bedaquiline both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. Benazepril increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. ACE inhibitors may increase the arrhythmogenic potential of ciprofloxacin, possibly by increasing serum potassium levels. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of bendamustine by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of a CYP1A2 inhibitor such as ciprofloxacin may increase bendamustine concentrations. Berotralstat increases the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and betamethasone may increase each other's toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of betaxolol by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider modifying therapy, as CYP1A2 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of 1A2 substrates. Biotin decreases the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 4 hours before or 2 hours after biotin. Use caution and monitor closely. Bosutinib increases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and buprenorphine (in all forms: buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of caffeine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The hepatic metabolism of caffeine may be decreased by ciprofloxacin, leading to increased pharmacologic effects of caffeine. Use caution and monitor closely. Calcium salts (acetate, carbonate, chloride, citrate, and gluconate) decrease the effects of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. Use caution and monitor closely. Captopril increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. ACE inhibitors increase the arrhythmogenic potential of ciprofloxacin. Monitor ECG and QT interval. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by reducing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. Carbonyl iron decreases the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of carvedilol by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Ciprofloxacin may also rarely decrease beta-blocker levels. Ciprofloxacin and celecoxib may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin and ceritinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Ciprofloxacin and chloroquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. Ciprofloxacin and chlorpromazine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. Ciprofloxacin decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Ciprofloxacin and citalopram both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with other drugs that may prolong the QT interval. Ciprofloxacin and clarithromycin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of drugs that can cause QT interval prolongation may result in additive effects and increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Monitor therapy carefully. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of clonazepam by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of clorazepate by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Use caution when administering ciprofloxacin in patients receiving drugs that prolong the QT interval. Clozapine and ciprofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concurrent short-term (14 days or less) use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable for patients taking cobimetinib 60 mg, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg. After discontinuation of a moderate CYP3A inhibitor, resume cobimetinib 60 mg. Use an alternative to a moderate CYP3A inhibitor in patients taking a reduced dose of cobimetinib (40 or 20 mg daily). Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of colchicine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Fatal drug interactions have been reported when colchicine is administered with dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Toxicities have also been reported when colchicine is administered with inhibitors of CYP3A4. Coadminister only if no other option is available. Contraindicated in renal or hepatic impairment with drugs that inhibit both P-gp and CYP3A4. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone.
